south dakota.rufada_status: South Dakota has adopted RUFADAA as the Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act in 2017 (House Bill 1080, Session Laws 2017, chapter 209). It is codified at South Dakota Codified Laws chapter 55-19, sections 55-19-1 through 55-19-27.
south dakota.custodian_access: A fiduciary — personal representative, trustee, agent under a power of attorney, or conservator — can get the catalogue of electronic communications (who the user communicated with, when, and the address) and other digital assets such as photos and files. The content of electronic communications, such as the text of emails, is disclosed only if the user consented to it or a court orders it. The custodian must comply within 60 days after receiving the required proof, may give full access, partial access, or a copy of the records, and may charge a reasonable administrative fee. It may require a written request, a death certificate, letters of appointment, a copy of the will, trust, or power of attorney, and an account identifier or other evidence linking the account to the user.
south dakota.user_direction: The user can direct disclosure through a custodian's online tool, naming a designated recipient, and can also allow or forbid disclosure in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other record. The priority order is: first the online tool, then the will, trust, or power of attorney, then the custodian's terms of service.
south dakota.terms_of_service: The custodian's terms of service cannot override a direction the user gave through an online tool or in a will, trust, or power of attorney. If the user left no direction, the terms of service can limit or eliminate the fiduciary's access, and the fiduciary then gets only what the statute allows without the user's consent to content, such as the catalogue of communications and other non-content digital assets.
south dakota.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets the user name up to ten trusted contacts and choose which data they receive after a chosen period of inactivity. Apple Legacy Contact lets the user name contacts who can request iCloud data with an access key and a death certificate. Meta (Facebook and Instagram) lets the user name a legacy contact to manage a memorialized profile, or choose deletion on death; the legacy contact cannot log in as the user or read private messages.
south dakota.what_to_do: First, make an inventory of accounts, devices, and crypto wallets and keys. Second, check whether the person set up an online tool such as Google Inactive Account Manager, Apple Legacy Contact, or a Meta legacy contact. Third, gather the will, trust, or power of attorney that names the fiduciary and gives digital-asset authority. Fourth, send each custodian a written request with a death certificate and proof of appointment. Fifth, if the custodian refuses or does not answer within 60 days, ask the probate court for an order directing disclosure.
south dakota.state_statute: South Dakota Codified Laws chapter 55-19, sections 55-19-1 through 55-19-27
south dakota.agency_name: South Dakota Attorney General, Division of Consumer Protection
south dakota.state_note: South Dakota placed its digital-assets law in Title 55, Fiduciaries and Trusts, rather than in the probate code, so the same chapter covers executors, trustees, agents, and conservators together.
sources: South Dakota Codified Laws section 55-19-6, Procedure for disclosing digital assets, at https://law.justia.com/codes/south-dakota/title-55/chapter-19/section-55-19-6/

wisconsin.rufada_status: Wisconsin has adopted the RUFADAA framework as the Wisconsin Digital Property Act in 2016 (2015 Assembly Bill 695, 2015 Act 300, signed March 30, 2016, effective April 1, 2016). It is codified at Wisconsin Statutes chapter 711, sections 711.01 through 711.15.
wisconsin.custodian_access: A fiduciary — personal representative, conservator or guardian, agent under a power of attorney, or trustee — can get the catalogue of electronic communications and other digital property. The content of electronic communications is disclosed only if the user affirmatively consented to it, through an online tool, a will or other governing instrument, or a written notarized consent instrument, or if a court orders it. The custodian must comply within 60 days after receiving the required proof, may give full access, partial access, or a copy of the records, and may charge a reasonable administrative fee. It may require a written request, a death certificate, letters of appointment, a copy of the will, trust, or power of attorney, and an account identifier or evidence linking the account to the user.
wisconsin.user_direction: The user can direct disclosure through a custodian's online tool, naming a designated recipient, and can also allow or forbid disclosure in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other record. The priority order is: first the online tool, then the will, trust, or power of attorney, then the custodian's terms of service. Wisconsin is distinctive in also recognizing a separate written notarized consent instrument for disclosure of message content.
wisconsin.terms_of_service: The custodian's terms of service cannot override a direction the user gave through an online tool or in a will, trust, or power of attorney. If the user left no direction, the terms of service can limit or eliminate the fiduciary's access, and the fiduciary then gets only the catalogue of communications and other non-content digital property that the statute allows.
wisconsin.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets the user name up to ten trusted contacts and choose which data they receive after a chosen period of inactivity. Apple Legacy Contact lets the user name contacts who can request iCloud data with an access key and a death certificate. Meta (Facebook and Instagram) lets the user name a legacy contact to manage a memorialized profile, or choose deletion on death; the legacy contact cannot log in as the user or read private messages.
wisconsin.what_to_do: First, make an inventory of accounts, devices, and crypto wallets and keys. Second, check whether the person set up an online tool such as Google Inactive Account Manager, Apple Legacy Contact, or a Meta legacy contact. Third, gather the will, trust, or power of attorney — or a notarized consent instrument — that names the fiduciary and gives digital-property authority, including express consent to message content if that access is needed. Fourth, send each custodian a written request with a death certificate and proof of appointment. Fifth, if the custodian refuses or does not answer within 60 days, ask the probate court for an order directing disclosure.
wisconsin.agency_name: Wisconsin Department of Justice, Consumer Protection
wisconsin.state_note: Wisconsin calls the subject digital property rather than digital assets, and it is the state in this set that expressly provides for a written notarized consent instrument as a way to authorize disclosure of the content of electronic communications.

wyoming.rufada_status: Wyoming has adopted the uniform fiduciary-access framework in 2016 (Senate File 34, chapter 39, signed March 7, 2016, effective July 1, 2016). It is codified at Wyoming Statutes sections 2-3-1001 through 2-3-1017 as the Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act.
wyoming.custodian_access: A fiduciary — personal representative, trustee, agent under a power of attorney, or conservator — can get the catalogue of electronic communications and other digital assets. The content of electronic communications is disclosed only if the user consented to it in an online tool or in a will, trust, or power of attorney, or if a court orders it. The custodian must comply within 60 days after receiving the required proof, may give full access, partial access, or a copy of the records, and may charge a reasonable administrative fee. It may require a written request, a death certificate, letters of appointment, a copy of the will, trust, or power of attorney, and an account identifier or evidence linking the account to the user.
wyoming.user_direction: The user can direct disclosure through a custodian's online tool, naming a designated recipient, and can also allow or forbid disclosure in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other record. The priority order is: first the online tool, then the will, trust, or power of attorney, then the custodian's terms of service.
wyoming.terms_of_service: The custodian's terms of service cannot override a direction the user gave through an online tool or in a will, trust, or power of attorney. If the user left no direction, the terms of service can limit or eliminate the fiduciary's access, and the fiduciary then gets only what the statute allows without the user's consent to content.
wyoming.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets the user name up to ten trusted contacts and choose which data they receive after a chosen period of inactivity. Apple Legacy Contact lets the user name contacts who can request iCloud data with an access key and a death certificate. Meta (Facebook and Instagram) lets the user name a legacy contact to manage a memorialized profile, or choose deletion on death; the legacy contact cannot log in as the user or read private messages.
wyoming.what_to_do: First, make an inventory of accounts, devices, and crypto wallets and keys. Second, check whether the person set up an online tool such as Google Inactive Account Manager, Apple Legacy Contact, or a Meta legacy contact. Third, gather the will, trust, or power of attorney that names the fiduciary and gives digital-asset authority. Fourth, send each custodian a written request with a death certificate and proof of appointment. Fifth, if the custodian refuses or does not answer within 60 days, ask the probate court for an order directing disclosure.
wyoming.agency_name: Wyoming Attorney General, Consumer Protection and Antitrust Unit
wyoming.state_note: Wyoming was one of the first three states to adopt the uniform act, in March 2016, and it later adopted separate laws on digital assets such as cryptocurrency, which are different from this fiduciary-access law and do not replace it.
sources: Wyoming Legislature, Senate File 34, 2016, Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act, sections 2-3-1001 through 2-3-1017, at https://wyoleg.gov/2016/Introduced/SF0034.pdf
